title: Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0070】Peroxisome-inspired biomaterials include enzyme-containing vesicles and catalytic hybrid assemblies designed to reproduce selected peroxisomal functions [19]. Antioxidant activity is presently a more established design objective than reconstruction of peroxisomal lipid metabolism. Patient-derived neural cultures, including neurons and glia, provide complementary systems in which to test material uptake, biochemical activity, and disease-associated phenotypes [20].

【Introduction · p0040】Neurodegenerative disorders (NDD) such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) rank among the leading causes of disability and death in ageing populations, and their incidence is projected to rise steeply over the coming decades [1]. These conditions, together with related pathologies including frontotemporal dementia, Huntington's disease, and various leukodystrophies, affect distinct but partially overlapping neural networks. AD primarily targets brain regions involved in memory and cognition, leading to progressive decline in thinking, behaviour, and independence, and is the leading cause of dementia worldwide [2]. PD is characterized mainly by motor symptoms such as tremor, slowness, and rigidity due to degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons, although many patients also develop non-motor symptoms, including cognitive impairment and sleep disturbances [3]. ALS predominantly affects motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord, causing progressive muscle weakness, paralysis, and ultimately respiratory failure, with most patients dying within a few years of diagnosis [4]. In parallel, several neurodevelopmental syndromes like Kleefstra syndrome (KS) and Rett syndrome (RTT) with prominent cognitive and psychiatric features exhibit early-life circuit dysfunction that often evolves on a background of chronic cellular stress [5], [6].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient-derived iPSC models in neurodegeneration and rare neurodevelopmental disorders · p0080】iPSC technology enables patient-specific neural differentiation and controlled investigation of genetic disease mechanisms [8], [21], [22]. Regionally patterned organoids can capture selected features of cortical, midbrain, or other neural tissues, but the cell types and level of organization depend on the protocol [23]. Studies of AD and PD illustrate how disease-associated protein processing and cellular vulnerability can be investigated in these systems [24], [25], [26]. Such models reproduce aspects of pathology rather than the full clinical disorder.

【Developmental sequence from material optimization to clinical testing · p0490】Development should proceed through explicit decision points (Fig. 1). Materials characterization must establish composition, size distribution, morphology, surface properties, permeability, retained active cargo, and stability. Cellular work should then demonstrate mechanistic activity, distinguish assay interference, and define a usable exposure range. Patient-derived neural validation should establish reproducibility and functional benefit in an appropriate model. Delivery studies should demonstrate intact material and catalytic activity beyond the relevant barrier and in the intended target population. Animal studies must relate biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, clearance, dose-response, and efficacy, with repeat-dose toxicology appropriate to the intended route and duration. Manufacturing development and regulatory consultation should begin early and continue alongside these stages. First-in-human consideration depends on a coherent benefit-risk package; success in an organoid alone is insufficient.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions and future perspectives · p0505】Peroxisomal functions are essential to neural biology, but their therapeutic relevance differs across disorders. Genetic and biochemical evidence establishes causality in primary peroxisomal diseases. In AD, PD, and ALS, the significance of reported abnormalities ranges from potentially contributory to unresolved. KS offers a model for testing a peroxisomal hypothesis rather than evidence of a peroxisome-driven disorder. Recent work has broadened the biological framework of Kleefstra syndrome beyond a neuron-centred model. In human iPSC-derived systems, EHMT1+/− astrocytes contributed directly to neuronal network dysfunction via astrocyte-dependent mechanisms linked to increased S100B signalling [196], while Drosophila lacking G9a, the functional orthologue of EHMT1, showed impaired oxidative stress tolerance with excessive glycogen depletion and defective lipid energy mobilization [197]. Neither study demonstrates a primary peroxisomal defect, but both implicate processes that overlap with established peroxisomal functions, including redox regulation, lipid metabolism, and metabolic stress responses. This strengthens the rationale for investigating peroxisome-related pathways in patient-derived KS models, while a causal link between EHMT1 haploinsufficiency and peroxisomal dysfunction remains to be established experimentally.

【Conclusions and future perspectives · p0510】Artificial-organelle studies demonstrate selected catalytic, transport, and targeting principles. They do not yet validate the integrated patient-derived CNS strategy discussed here. Patient-derived neural cultures can test mechanistic activity, cell interactions, and functional outcomes, while their incomplete maturation, donor variability, and transport constraints must remain part of interpretation.

Patient-derived neural cultures can test mechanistic activity, cell interactions, and functional outcomes, while their incomplete maturation, donor variability, and transport constraints must remain part of interpretation.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 Proposed evaluation framework for peroxisome-inspired CNS biomaterials. (A) Disease selection distinguishes primary peroxisomal disorders, late-onset neurodegeneration, and KS as a hypothesis-generating developmental context. (B) Patient-derived neural systems enable disease phenotyping and measurement of peroxisomal function. Neural progenitor-derived spheroids and cerebral organoids are distinct model types. (C) Material composition, retained catalytic cargo, permeability, and validated surface ligands are selected for a defined mechanism. Antioxidant activity and lipid-metabolic replacement require different evidence. (D) Neural efficacy, BBB transport, animal pharmacology, safety, and manufacturing are evaluated through decision points with iteration between stages. Progression is conditional on reproducible target engagement, functional benefit, exposure, and acceptable safety. The diagram describes a proposed development process, not a validated therapeutic pipeline. Figure was created with BioRender.com.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Peroxisomal mechanisms and disease-specific interpretation. (A) Peroxisomes contribute to fatty acid processing, the initial steps of ether-lipid synthesis, and H2O2 production and removal. Their interactions with mitochondria involve metabolic and redox coupling, while plasmalogen biosynthesis also requires the endoplasmic reticulum. Shared fission machinery and reported contacts do not establish universal directional substrate or Ca2+ transfer. (B) Peroxisomal defects are causal in primary peroxisomal disorders; AD evidence is largely associative, the causal position in PD and ALS remains uncertain, and KS requires direct peroxisomal phenotyping. (C) A disease-associated defect must be linked to a specific material function and an independent functional outcome. Demonstrated antioxidant catalysis should be distinguished from proposed lipid-metabolic restoration. Arrows indicate relationships or proposed evaluation steps, not established causal chains in all diseases. Figure was created with BioRender.com.

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 Material design and catalytic transport in artificial peroxisomes. (A) Liposomal, polymeric, and hybrid membranes provide different options for composition, permeability, stability, and degradation. These properties require measurement for each formulation. (B) H2O2 must access catalase while active enzyme is retained. OmpF illustrates a pore-forming design precedent, not a validated component of every platform. SOD converts accessible superoxide to H2O2, requiring sufficient downstream peroxide removal. H2O2, superoxide, and hydroxyl radical are distinct chemical species with different transport and reaction behaviour. (C) Stimuli-responsive materials require an experimentally demonstrated link between trigger, structural response, and catalytic performance. (D) Relevant measurements include hydrodynamic size, charge, membrane mechanics, ligand density, active loading, leakage, permeability, and degradation. No universal size or charge optimum for CNS delivery is implied. Figure was created with BioRender.com.
